note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with dysuria and urinary frequency for 3 days.
The patient reports dysuria and frequency occurring about every 30 minutes since Saturday.
The patient reported possible pink-tinged urine this morning.
The patient denies loin pain, fever, rigors, nausea, or vomiting.
The patient denies vaginal discharge or itching.
The patient has a history of one previous UTI two years ago, which was treated with antibiotics (agent unknown).
The patient's period is approximately one week late, and no pregnancy test has been performed yet.
The patient has no known renal disease.
The patient takes Vitamin D during the winter.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The examination was a telephone consultation, and the patient was speaking in full sentences and sounded well.
The clinical impression is a lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
Possible early pregnancy is noted and needs to be excluded.
The prescribed treatment is Nitrofurantoin 100 mg modified-release capsules, twice daily for 7 days.
A pregnancy test is ordered today.
A urine sample is requested for culture before starting antibiotics.
The patient is advised to drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol for discomfort.
Ibuprofen should be avoided until pregnancy is excluded.
The patient should call the practice or 111 immediately if they develop back/side pain, fever, shivering, or vomiting.
The patient should call back if they do not feel better within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or if symptoms worsen.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Whitlock calling back from the surgery.
Patient is at home.
Patient's date of birth is the second of November, 1997.
Patient reports burning when urinating (dysuria) and needing to go every half an hour (frequency).
The patient reports the symptoms have been going on since Saturday, which is three days now.
Patient reports maybe a little pinkish urine this morning.
Patient denies any pain in the back or sides, just under the ribs.
Patient denies fever, shivers, or shakes, stating they feel okay.
Patient denies feeling sick or vomiting.
Patient denies unusual vaginal discharge or itching.
Patient had a previous UTI about two years ago, which cleared up after treatment with antibiotics (agent unknown).
Patient states they don't think they are pregnant but their period is about a week late.
Patient has not yet done a pregnancy test.
Patient takes Vitamin D in the winter.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient denies any problems with their kidneys.
Clinician suggests the condition sounds like a urine infection in the bladder (cystitis).
Clinician prescribes Nitrofurantoin 100 milligrams, modified-release capsules, twice a day for seven days.
Clinician requests the patient do a pregnancy test today and drop a urine sample before starting antibiotics.
Clinician instructs the patient to ring back tomorrow with the pregnancy test result, and if positive, a face-to-face review and treatment plan change will occur.
Clinician advises the patient to drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol for discomfort.
Clinician advises sticking to paracetamol for now until pregnancy status is known.
Clinician warns that developing back/side pain, fever, shivering, or vomiting could mean the infection has spread to the kidneys, and advises calling immediately or 111 if closed.
Clinician instructs the patient to call back if they are not starting to feel better within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or if they are getting worse.
